why: Redis 单线程主要指命令执行器串行触碰数据结构，因此不需要数据库式行锁。多核能跑旁路工作，但不会拆分单条 SET/INCR。
why_en: Redis single-threaded mostly means the command executor touches data structures serially, so it does not need database-style row locks. Extra cores can run side work, but one SET/INCR is not split apart.

  execute_command(cmd)     # GET/SET/INCR touch Redis data here
  enqueue_reply(cmd)

# Helper threads may read sockets, parse protocol, or write replies.
# They do not run the same key's SET/INCR body in parallel.

scenario: 你在 redis-cli 里敲 SET name alice。客户端真正发到 Redis TCP 连接上的不是 HTTP 请求，而是一段 RESP 编码。

options: 二进制列式编码

why: RESP 是 Redis 客户端和服务器在 TCP 上说话的线格式：简单、快解析、基本可读，且不是 HTTP/gRPC。
why_en: RESP is the wire format Redis clients and servers speak over TCP: simple, fast to parse, mostly readable, and not HTTP/gRPC.
options_en: A binary columnar encoding
Commands and arguments travel over the wire almost exactly as you type them
A gRPC protocol layered on HTTP/2
You must go through an ORM framework to access it
codeSample:
# What you type:
SET name alice

# What the client sends over TCP as RESP:
*3\r\n
$3\r\nSET\r\n
$4\r\nname\r\n
$5\r\nalice\r\n

# Redis reply:
+OK\r\n

flowchart LR
  CLI["redis-cli: SET name alice"] --> Enc["RESP encode"]
  Enc --> TCP["TCP socket"]
  TCP --> R["Redis server"]

  Exec --> Resp["+OK CRLF"]

termDefinitions.meaning: RESP（REdis Serialization Protocol）：Redis 客户端和服务器之间的 wire protocol，用前缀和长度把命令、参数、返回值编码成字节流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RESP, or REdis Serialization Protocol, is the wire protocol between Redis clients and servers, using prefixes and lengths to encode commands, arguments, and replies as bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: wire protocol：程序在网络连接上实际传输的字节格式；这里常被中文说成线上协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wire protocol is the byte format programs actually send over a network connection; this is what 'online protocol' refers to here.

termDefinitions.meaning: bulk string：RESP 里带长度前缀的字符串，例如 $5\r\nhello\r\n；可安全传二进制内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bulk string is a length-prefixed RESP string, such as $5\r\nhello\r\n, and can safely carry binary data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CRLF：\r\n，RESP 用它分隔协议片段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRLF means \r\n, the separator RESP uses between protocol parts.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/2：支持多路复用的第二代 HTTP 协议，Redis 并不用它做线上协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second major HTTP version with multiplexing, and it is not the protocol Redis speaks.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC：基于 HTTP/2 和 Protobuf 的远程调用框架，与 RESP 无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a remote-procedure-call framework built on HTTP/2 and Protobuf, unrelated to Redis's RESP protocol.

termDefinitions.meaning: ORM（对象关系映射）：把数据库行映射成程序对象的框架，Redis 访问不需要它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ORM, or Object-Relational Mapping, maps database rows to program objects, and Redis access does not require one.

q: 「先抢锁再干活」和 Redis 的 WATCH + MULTI/EXEC 分别属于哪种并发控制？
options: 两者都属于乐观并发控制，不阻塞其他客户端
前者悲观；后者乐观——被 WATCH 的 key 中途变了，事务就中止

why: 先抢锁是悲观并发控制：先把别人挡在外面。WATCH+MULTI/EXEC 是乐观并发控制：允许别人同时写，但 EXEC 时如果 watched key 已变化，就返回失败并重试。
why_en: Grabbing a lock up front is pessimistic because others must wait. WATCH with MULTI/EXEC is optimistic: other clients can still write, but EXEC aborts if the watched key changed.

SET lock:stock:item:1 workerA NX PX 30000
DECR stock:item:1
DEL lock:stock:item:1

# Optimistic: watch, compute, then commit conditionally.
retry:
  WATCH stock:item:1
  old = GET stock:item:1
  if old <= 0:
    UNWATCH
    return sold_out

  MULTI
    SET stock:item:1 old - 1
  ok = EXEC          # nil/null if stock:item:1 changed after WATCH

  if ok == null:
    goto retry       # someone else changed it; reread and recompute

    Note over P: 崩溃(锁未复制出去)
    R->>R: 被提升为新主
    C2->>R: SET lock NX EX (也成功!)
    Note over C1,C2: 两个客户端同时持锁
options_en: The primary dies before the lock replicates, so the promoted replica grants the same lock again
The lock key gets migrated to the wrong slot
The lock's TTL accidentally resets to zero
The replica refuses every lock request
tradeoff: 单节点 Redis 锁简单低延迟 vs failover 可能破坏互斥

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点先回 OK，副本之后才追复制流；中间有一个丢尾部写入的窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary replies OK first and replicas apply the replication stream later, leaving a window where tail writes can be lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点故障后，把副本提升成新的主节点继续服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover promotes a replica to become the new primary after the old primary fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 加锁常见写法：key 不存在才写入，并给锁设置过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A common Redis lock command: set only if the key does not exist, with an expiry time.

q_en: What's the classic way a single-node Redis lock fails during primary-replica failover?
scenario_en: Client C1 acquires a lock on the Redis primary with SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000. The primary replies OK, but the lock record has not replicated to the replica before the primary crashes.
optionMeanings: 正确失败链：旧主已回 OK，但新主没见过这把锁。
把主从 failover 误解成 Cluster slot 迁移。
把问题误放到 TTL 配置变化。
误以为副本升主后不会服务写请求。
optionDirectness: 正确：新主没有 lock key，所以第二个 SET NX 可成功。
不对：这题不是 Redis Cluster 槽位问题。
不对：TTL 没被改也会失效。
不对：副本被提升后就是新的 primary。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会出现两个客户端都以为自己持锁。
会把排查方向带到 hash slot，而不是复制延迟。
会误以为调 TTL 就能解决 failover 丢锁。
会低估 failover 后新主继续接写的事实。
optionMeanings_en: The real failure chain: the old primary replied OK, but the new primary never saw the lock.
Confuses primary-replica failover with Cluster slot migration.
Moves the issue to an accidental TTL change.
Assumes the promoted replica will not serve writes.
optionDirectness_en: Correct: the new primary has no lock key, so a second SET NX can succeed.
Wrong: this is not a Redis Cluster slot issue.
Wrong: the failure happens even if TTL was not changed.
Wrong: once promoted, the replica is the new primary.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two clients can both believe they hold the lock.
It sends debugging toward hash slots instead of replication lag.
It suggests TTL tuning can fix failover lock loss.
It underestimates that the new primary keeps accepting writes.

scenario: 你要保护 order:123，同一时间只能一个 worker 处理。注意这不是 Redis Cluster 分片；Redlock 会把同一个 lock key 发给 5 个独立 Redis，至少 3 个同意才算拿到锁。
scenario_en: You need to protect order:123 so only one worker handles it at a time. This is not Redis Cluster sharding; Redlock sends the same lock key to five independent Redis nodes and succeeds only if at least three agree.
q: Redlock 算法的核心思路是？
options: 只是把锁的 TTL 设得比原来更长一些
在多数（quorum）个互不复制的独立 Redis 节点上都拿到锁才算成功
把锁写进 AOF 日志并强制立即刷盘
用 hash tag 把锁强制绑到某个固定槽位
why: Cluster 是 key→一个槽；Redlock 是同一锁 key→多个 Redis。多数 SET NX 成功且未超 TTL 才算拿锁。
why_en: Cluster maps a key to one slot; Redlock sends the same lock key to several independent Redis nodes. The lock is acquired only if a majority SET NX succeeds before TTL expires.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["worker A"] --> R1["Redis 1 OK"]
    C --> R2["Redis 2 OK"]
    C --> R3["Redis 3 OK"]
    C -.timeout.-> R4["Redis 4"]
    C -.down.-> R5["Redis 5"]
    R1 --> Q["3/5 quorum"]
    R2 --> Q
    R3 --> Q
    Q --> OK["lease acquired"]
options_en: Just set the lock's TTL to something longer than before
Acquire the lock on a majority (quorum) of independent, non-replicating Redis nodes
Write the lock into the AOF log and force an immediate fsync
Use a hash tag to pin the lock to one fixed slot

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是多数派；5 个节点至少 3 个，3 个节点至少 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is a majority: at least three of five nodes, or two of three nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 分布式锁算法：同一个 lock key 写到多个独立 Redis，拿到多数才成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis distributed lock algorithm that writes the same lock key to several independent Redis nodes and succeeds with a majority.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 算 slot，一个 key 只归一个主节点；这是容量分片，不是 Redlock 的多数裁决。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster hashes each key to one slot and one primary; that is capacity sharding, not Redlock quorum voting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有过期时间的锁；只在 TTL 剩余窗口内有效，过期后别人可以重新抢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-limited lock that is valid only within its TTL window; after expiry, another client may acquire it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次抢锁写入的唯一值；释放时先比对 token，避免删掉别人的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A unique value written during acquisition; release compares the token first so it does not delete someone else's lock.

termDefinitions.term: 互不复制的独立 Redis 节点
termDefinitions.meaning: 这些节点不是同一主从组；一个节点丢锁不会变成主从切换丢锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Independent Redis nodes are not replicas, so one node losing a lock is not a replica-failover lock loss.

q_en: What is the core idea behind the Redlock algorithm?
optionMeanings: 拉长 TTL：让锁更晚过期，但还是只有一个 Redis 判断。
多数派 Redlock：同一个 token 要写入多数独立节点。
AOF 强刷：把单节点锁尽量写牢到磁盘。
hash tag 固槽：这是 Cluster 同槽技巧，不是 Redlock。
optionDirectness: 只想减少任务超时误释放时，拉长 TTL 有帮助。
要降低单节点 failover 丢锁风险时，才是 Redlock 核心。
只担心单机崩溃后的持久化窗口时，AOF 更相关。
多 key 要同槽执行 Lua/事务时，hash tag 才有用。
optionScenarioImpacts: 单 Redis 仍可能 failover 后丢锁，长 TTL 不能形成多数裁决。
两个客户端的多数派会相交，重叠节点挡住双重持锁。
它加强单节点持久性，但没有跨多个独立节点投票。
它解决 Cluster 路由，不产生多数派裁决。
optionMeanings_en: Longer TTL: the lock expires later, but one Redis node still decides.
Majority Redlock: the same token must be written to a majority of independent nodes.
AOF fsync: make a single-node lock more durable on disk.
Hash tag slot pinning: a Cluster co-location trick, not Redlock.
optionDirectness_en: Useful when the main problem is a task outliving a short TTL.
Use this when reducing single-node failover lock loss is the goal.
Relevant when the concern is the persistence window of one node.
Useful when multiple keys must share one slot for Lua or transactions.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: One Redis can still lose the lock after failover; TTL length is not a vote.
Two clients' majorities must intersect, so the shared node blocks double ownership.
It improves one node's durability but does not create multi-node agreement.
It solves Cluster routing, not quorum voting.

scenario: worker A 用 Redlock 拿到 order:123 的 30 秒租约后卡住 45 秒；锁过期后 worker B 拿到新锁并写入。A 醒来时，本地还拿着旧锁结果。
q: Kleppmann 对 Redlock 的著名批评指出：即使算法成立，仍会发生什么？
options: N 个节点里多数派永远无法达成，算法根本跑不起来
所有参与节点的时钟必须做到精确同步
客户端 GC 暂停或卡顿后，会拿着已经过期的锁继续操作
获取锁的吞吐量在多节点方案下太低，扛不住并发
why: Redlock 只管“谁拿到租约”；租约过期后，旧持有者可能醒来继续写。资源端若不查 fencing token/版本号，旧写仍能覆盖新写。
why_en: Redlock decides who acquired the lease, but after the lease expires a stale holder can wake up and keep writing. Without a fencing token or version check at the resource, an old write can overwrite a newer one.
codeSample:
A = redlock.acquire("order:123", ttl=30s)
pause(A, 45s)          # GC / scheduler / network delay

B = redlock.acquire("order:123", ttl=30s)
DB.write(order=123, status="paid-by-B")

# A wakes up after its lease expired.
DB.write(order=123, status="paid-by-A")  # unsafe unless DB rejects stale token
options_en: A majority of the N nodes can never be reached, so the algorithm cannot even run
Every participating node's clock must be kept in perfect sync
A paused or slow client can resume acting after its lock has already expired
The lock's acquisition throughput is too low across multiple nodes to handle real concurrency
tradeoff: Redlock 多数派拿锁 vs 资源端 fencing 才能挡旧写
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant L as Redlock
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database
  A->>L: acquire lease 30s
  Note over A: paused 45s
  B->>L: acquire new lease
  B->>DB: write with new state
  A->>DB: wakes and writes stale state
  Note over DB: reject only if token/version is checked

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 分布式锁算法：向多个独立 Redis 节点抢锁，拿到多数才算成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis distributed lock algorithm that acquires a lock on a majority of independent Redis nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC（垃圾回收）：运行时自动回收内存的过程，期间进程可能暂停一段时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GC, or garbage collection, is the runtime's automatic memory cleanup, which can pause a process for a while.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单调递增的授锁编号；数据库/存储只接受比已记录编号更新的写入，用来挡旧持有者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An increasing lock-grant number; storage accepts only newer tokens to reject stale holders.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有过期时间的锁；过期后别人可以重新获得同一资源的资格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock with an expiry time; after expiry, another client may acquire the same resource.

q_en: Kleppmann's famous critique of Redlock says that even if the algorithm holds, what can still happen?
scenario_en: Worker A acquires a 30-second Redlock lease for order:123, then stalls for 45 seconds. After the lock expires, worker B acquires a new lock and writes. When A wakes up, it still has its old local lock result.
optionMeanings: 误以为 Redlock 多数派无法工作。
误以为批评点是要求完美同步时钟。
正确：旧持有者暂停太久，醒来后继续写。
误以为主要问题是吞吐，而非正确性。
optionDirectness: 不对：多数派可能达成。
不对：问题是时间假设和旧写，不是要完美同步。
正确：锁服务挡不住过期后的客户端写数据库。
不对：吞吐不是 Kleppmann 的核心批评。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会把 Redlock 误解成完全不可运行。
会忽略进程暂停和网络延迟也能制造旧写。
会引出 fencing token 或数据层条件写。
会把正确性问题误当性能调优。
optionMeanings_en: Incorrectly assumes Redlock majorities cannot work.
Incorrectly makes perfect clock sync the main criticism.
Correct: an old holder can pause too long and then keep writing.
Incorrectly frames the issue as throughput rather than correctness.
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: a majority can be reached.
Wrong: the issue is timing assumptions and stale writes, not perfect sync.
Correct: the lock service cannot stop an expired client from writing to the database.
Wrong: throughput is not Kleppmann's central critique.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It misreads Redlock as unable to run at all.
It misses that process pauses and network delay can also create stale writes.
It leads to fencing tokens or data-layer conditional writes.
It treats a correctness risk as a performance-tuning issue.

scenario: 支付/库存服务用 Redis 锁保护 order:123：worker A 拿到 30 秒锁后开始处理，但因为 GC、网络卡顿或外部 API 慢暂停了 45 秒。锁自动过期后，worker B 又拿到锁并写入了正确的新状态。此时 A 醒来，如果它还直接写数据库，就会用旧判断覆盖 B 的结果。
scenario_en: A payment or inventory service protects order:123 with a Redis lock. Worker A gets a 30-second lock but pauses for 45 seconds because of GC, network delay, or a slow external API. The lock expires, worker B acquires it and writes the correct newer state. If A wakes up and still writes the database, it can overwrite B with stale data.
q: 防止「过期锁的持有者继续写坏数据」的标准手段是？
options: 让持有者每隔几秒就主动给锁续租延长时限
简单粗暴地把锁的 TTL 加大十倍来兜底
同时申请两把互相独立的锁做双重保险来兜底
fencing token：每次授锁附带递增编号，存储层拒绝旧编号的写入
why: 锁过期不会让旧 worker 自动停。每次授锁发递增 fencing token，写 DB 时带 token；B 的 18 写入后，A 的 17 会被存储层拒绝，续租或加长 TTL 只能降概率。
why_en: An expired Redis lock cannot stop the old worker, so each grant needs a higher fencing token and storage must reject stale tokens.
whenOtherWins: 如果过期后最多只是重复做一次幂等小任务，比如重复刷新缓存，Redis 锁加随机 token 通常够用；只要会影响钱、库存、唯一状态、leader 写入，就要让数据层检查 fencing token 或版本号。
options_en: Have the holder proactively renew the lock's lease every few seconds to extend it
Just brute-force the lock's TTL to ten times longer as a safety net
Acquire two mutually independent locks at once as a double safeguard
A fencing token: each grant carries an increasing number, and storage rejects writes stamped with an old one
tradeoff: Redis 锁的简单互斥 vs 数据层 fencing 的真正防旧写能力
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 request-A NX PX 30000
INCR lock_token:order:123   # returns 17

# Storage, not Redis, rejects stale holders.
UPDATE orders
SET status = :status, last_fencing_token = :token
WHERE id = :order_id
  AND :token > last_fencing_token;
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis lock
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database or storage
  A->>R: SET NX PX succeeds, token 17
  Note over A: pauses longer than TTL
  B->>R: SET NX PX succeeds, token 18
  B->>DB: write with token 18
  DB-->>B: accept and record last_token=18
  A->>DB: stale write with token 17
  DB-->>A: reject

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token：每次授锁都附带的单调递增编号，资源端只接受比已记录编号更新的写入，用来隔离旧持有者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is an increasing number issued with each lock grant that storage uses to reject writes from a stale holder.

termDefinitions.meaning: lock value：Redis 锁里常放的随机 requestId，用来释放锁时确认「这把锁还是我的」。它防误删，不防过期后的旧写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock value is a random requestId stored in the Redis lock so a client deletes only its own lock. It prevents accidental unlocks, not stale writes after expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS：带条件的写入，只有版本号、token 或旧值匹配时才更新；SQL 的 WHERE version/token 条件和 DynamoDB ConditionExpression 都是常见形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS, or compare-and-set, updates only if a version, token, or previous value condition still matches; SQL conditional updates and DynamoDB ConditionExpression are common forms.

q_en: What's the standard technique to stop an expired lock's holder from corrupting data with a stale write?
optionMeanings: 续租只是延长租约。
加大 TTL 只是降低过期概率。
双锁增加复杂度但不挡旧写。
fencing token 让存储层识别旧持有者。
optionDirectness: 适合任务可续心跳、偶发超时可接受。
适合只想减少误过期的非关键任务。
只有两个独立资源都要保护时才有意义。
钱、库存、leader 写入要选它。
optionScenarioImpacts: A 暂停超过租约时仍可能醒来旧写。
45 秒 GC 仍可能超过更长 TTL。
A 醒来写 DB 时两把锁都帮不上忙。
DB 用 token 顺序拒绝 A 的旧结果。
optionMeanings_en: Renewal only extends the lease.
A longer TTL only lowers expiry probability.
Two locks add complexity but do not block stale writes.
A fencing token lets storage identify stale holders.
optionDirectness_en: Use renewal when heartbeat failure is acceptable.
Use a longer TTL only for non-critical probability reduction.
Use two locks only when two independent resources need protection.
Use this for money, inventory, or leader writes.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A can still wake after the lease and write stale data.
A long GC pause can still outlive the larger TTL.
The database write is still unguarded when A wakes.
Storage rejects A by token order.

scenario: 同一张票、同一笔订单、同一个司机派单，同一时刻只能被一个 worker 处理。Redis 锁通常就是一个带 TTL 的 key，例如 SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000；A 拿到锁表示 30 秒内别人先别处理 order:123。问题是锁存在 Redis 里，真实业务数据通常在 MySQL/DynamoDB/S3/外部支付系统里，锁过期不会自动让 A 的代码停下来，也不会自动阻止 A 继续写下游。
q: 正确的态度是？
options: 把 TTL 直接加长到 10 分钟
上 Redlock 就万无一失
把 Redis 锁当作正确性的基石
Redis 锁只当效率优化；正确性靠数据层约束或共识系统
why: Redis 锁只能减少并发，不能让过期持有者停手；A 暂停、锁过期、B 写新状态后，A 醒来仍可能写下游。所以钱、库存、唯一状态要由 DB 条件写、版本号或 fencing token 拒绝旧写。
why_en: Use Redis locks as a concurrency throttle, but enforce money, inventory, and uniqueness invariants in storage with conditional writes, versions, or fencing tokens.
whenOtherWins: 若锁失效的后果只是重复做一点幂等工作（如重复刷新缓存、重复预热一个可再生结果），Redis 锁完全够用，不必引入 ZooKeeper 的复杂度。
options_en: Just extend the TTL to ten minutes
Adding Redlock makes it foolproof
Treat the Redis lock as the foundation of correctness
Treat a Redis lock as an efficiency tool; enforce correctness with data-layer constraints or a consensus system
tradeoff: Redis 锁的效率 vs 数据层/共识系统的正确性保证
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000

# Unsafe after the lock expires:
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid' WHERE id = 123;

# Source of truth checks state/token.
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'paid', fencing_token = :token
WHERE id = 123 AND status = 'reserved'
  AND :token > fencing_token;
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database
  A->>R: SET lock NX PX 30s succeeds
  Note over A: pause / GC / slow API for 45s
  Note over R: lock expires
  B->>R: SET lock NX PX succeeds
  B->>DB: write correct new state
  A->>DB: wakes up and writes stale state
  Note over DB: Redis cannot block this write unless DB checks version/token

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：用 Redis 里的一个 key 表示某个资源暂时被占用，常见写法是 SET lock:resource requestId NX PX ttl。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock uses a Redis key to represent temporary ownership of a resource, commonly SET lock:resource requestId NX PX ttl.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过期锁持有者：曾经拿到锁、但锁的 TTL 已经过期的进程；它本地可能还以为自己有资格继续写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An expired lock holder is a process that once acquired the lock but whose TTL has expired; locally it may still believe it can keep writing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 资损：钱、库存、订单状态等业务资产被错误扣减、重复扣减或错误覆盖造成的损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Financial loss means business assets such as money, inventory, or order state are incorrectly decremented, duplicated, or overwritten.

termDefinitions.meaning: invariant：系统必须永远成立的业务规则，例如一张票只能卖一次、一笔订单只能扣款一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a business rule that must always hold, such as one ticket can be sold once or one order can be charged once.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper：基于共识协议的分布式协调服务，可提供强一致的锁语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-based distributed coordination service that can provide strongly consistent locking.

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd：另一个基于 Raft 共识的分布式键值存储，常用来做强一致协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-based distributed key-value store commonly used for strongly consistent coordination.

q_en: What's the right attitude to take?
scenario_en: The same ticket, order, or driver dispatch must be handled by only one worker at a time. A Redis lock is usually a TTL key such as SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000; A getting the lock means other workers should not process order:123 for 30 seconds. But the lock lives in Redis, while real business data often lives in MySQL, DynamoDB, S3, or an external payment system. Lock expiry does not automatically stop A's code or block A from writing downstream.
optionMeanings: 长 TTL 只把问题往后推。
Redlock 仍挡不住过期持有者写下游。
把互斥误当成业务正确性。
Redis 锁负责少并发，数据层负责正确性。
optionDirectness: 适合非关键任务减少误过期。
适合想降低单 Redis failover 风险。
只有下游写天然幂等/可覆盖时才勉强。
跨系统状态和资损风险下选它。
optionScenarioImpacts: A 仍可能超过更长 TTL 后旧写。
A 醒来写 DB 时 Redlock 不在 DB 内。
会让库存/支付覆盖风险漏到生产。
旧写被版本、条件或 token 拦住。
optionMeanings_en: A longer TTL only postpones the issue.
Redlock still cannot stop an expired holder from writing downstream.
This mistakes mutual exclusion for business correctness.
Redis reduces concurrency; storage enforces correctness.
optionDirectness_en: Use this only to reduce false expiry for non-critical work.
Use Redlock to reduce single-Redis failover risk, not stale writes.
Only tolerable when downstream writes are idempotent or harmless.

why_en: Pub/Sub only notifies subscribers that are online right now; offline catch-up must read from a durable log/queue or Message+Inbox tables. An outbox table is often used to make 'write the message' and 'publish the event later' reliable.
whenOtherWins: 若消息只对「此刻在场」的人有意义（光标位置、正在输入提示），纯 Pub/Sub 反而是最省的正确答案；若已用 Kafka 做实时消费，也可以不用 Redis Pub/Sub。

  msg = Messages.insert(chatId, senderId, body)

  Outbox.insert(type="MessageCreated", msgId=msg.id, chatId=chatId)
  tx.commit()

    redis.publish("chat:" + event.chatId, { "msgId": event.msgId })
    Outbox.markSent(event.id)

q: 「自制 Pub/Sub」（Redis 里存 topic → 订阅者地址集合，发布者自己逐个直发）相比原生 Pub/Sub 的缺点有哪些？（多选）
options: 网络跳数从 2 跳变成 3 跳
发布者要维护到订阅者服务器的连接；没有连接池就要临时建 TCP/TLS
订阅者宕机后要靠心跳/TTL 清理注册表，复杂且啰嗦
发布的消息体大小会受到限制
why: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 chat server 到 Redis 的 TCP/TLS 连接，Redis 维护订阅并 push。自制只让 Redis 存地址，发布者查表后自己 fanout；连接池、重试、背压和旧地址清理都归应用。
why_en: Native Pub/Sub still uses TCP/TLS, but it reuses established Redis client connections from chat servers to Redis; Redis maintains channel-to-connection state and pushes over those connections. In a homegrown design, Redis only stores addresses, so the publisher fans out itself and owns server-to-server pools, TLS, retries, backpressure, health checks, and stale-address cleanup.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有一套成熟的 service mesh、长连接池、健康检查和路由层，自制直发可以降低 Redis 数据面压力；但这时你其实是在重建一个消息路由系统，复杂度要算进去。

The publisher must maintain connections to subscriber servers; without a pool it pays TCP/TLS setup
A dead subscriber needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean up the registry, which is complex and chatty
The published message body size becomes limited
tradeoff: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 Redis 的订阅连接/生命周期管理 vs 自制方案把路由和清理责任推给应用

# Redis pushes to subscribers on their existing Redis connections.

# Homegrown registry: Redis stores addresses, not live Pub/Sub pipes.
SADD topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000 chat-server-b:9000
SMEMBERS topic:room:123:subscribers

# Publisher must fan out server-to-server itself.
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-a:9000", message)
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-b:9000", message)

# It must also clean stale subscriber addresses.
SET subscriber:chat-server-a:9000:heartbeat 1 EX 30
SREM topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000  # when lease expires

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP（传输控制协议）：建立连接后可靠传输字节流的协议，新建连接有握手开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP, or Transmission Control Protocol, is a connection-based reliable byte-stream protocol whose handshake adds setup cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis client connection：应用服务器到 Redis 的已建立连接；SUBSCRIBE 后 Redis 会在这条连接上持续推送消息。

termDefinitions.meaning: TLS：给 TCP 连接加密和校验身份的一层；Redis 可以配置 TLS 端口，但这不改变 Pub/Sub 的订阅模型。

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat/TTL：订阅者定期续租自己的注册记录；如果停止续租，系统认为它已死并清理地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat/TTL lease means subscribers periodically refresh their registry entry; if they stop, the system treats them as dead and cleans up the address.

whenOtherWins: 如果目标只是别打爆 Redis primary，显式副本读或 key 副本也对；如果库存、余额这类不能陈旧，就不要用本地 TTL 缓存做正确性来源。

Just give the Redis node that owns the hot key more memory
Switch the persistence mode from RDB to AOF
Increase the cluster's total hash slot count beyond 16384

    redis.setex("product:" + id, 30s, v)

q: 集群模式下多 key 操作（MSET、含多个 key 的 MULTI）的限制是？

Use a shared hash tag when those keys must be operated on together.

scenario: Postgres/MySQL 这类数据库允许你写一条比较抽象的 SQL：查用户、过滤状态、按时间排序、再 join 订单表。数据库会先生成多个可能的执行方案，再选一个预计最便宜的方案。Redis 不走这条路：你要提前把数据放成合适的结构，比如 String、Hash、Set、Sorted Set，然后直接调用 GET/HGET/ZRANGE 这类明确命令。
scenario_en: Databases such as Postgres or MySQL let you write a fairly abstract SQL query: find users, filter by status, sort by time, and join an orders table. The database generates possible execution strategies and chooses the estimated cheapest one. Redis does not work this way: you pre-shape data into structures such as String, Hash, Set, or Sorted Set, then call explicit commands such as GET, HGET, or ZRANGE.
q: 相比自带优化器和查询计划器的数据库，Redis 的取向是？
options: 追求比别人更智能的自动优化

why: Redis 不像 SQL 数据库那样替你规划 join、索引选择和排序路径；GET/HGET/ZRANGE 的访问路径由数据结构决定。好处是性能透明、命令快；代价是复杂查询和二级索引要提前建模。
why_en: Redis favors explicit data-structure access over SQL-style planning, which keeps commands predictable but pushes joins, secondary indexes, and complex queries into your model.
options_en: Chasing smarter automatic optimization than everyone else
Deliberately staying simple: make simple operations very fast and leave composition to you
Hiding every implementation detail from you
Designed around complex analytical queries
tradeoff: 数据库自动规划复杂查询 vs Redis 明确数据结构带来的可预测性能

scenario: Redis 是纯内存存储，重启会丢数据，靠 RDB 快照或 AOF 日志落盘持久化。
scenario_en: Redis keeps data in memory and loses it on restart, so it persists to disk via either RDB snapshots or the AOF log.
q: 关于 RDB 与 AOF 的对比，下面哪个说法正确？
q_en: Which statement about RDB vs AOF is correct?
options: AOF 丢数据窗口更小，RDB 恢复更快
RDB 记录每条写命令，AOF 存周期性全量二进制快照
两者都只把数据放在内存里、根本不写磁盘
AOF 与 RDB 都靠 SSTable 合并来压缩体积
options_en: AOF loses less data on a crash; RDB restores faster
RDB logs every write command while AOF stores periodic full snapshots
Both keep data only in memory and never write to disk
Both AOF and RDB rely on SSTable compaction to shrink in size
why: RDB = 周期性全量二进制快照，恢复快但会丢上次快照后的写；AOF = 顺序追加每条写命令、重放恢复，就是 Redis 的 WAL，最多丢约 1 秒。二者可同时开：AOF 保命 + RDB 快恢复。
why_en: RDB is a periodic full snapshot: fast restore but loses writes since the last one. AOF appends every write and replays on restart — Redis's WAL, losing ~1s. You can run both.
tradeoff: RDB（恢复快 / 可能丢更多） vs AOF（丢得少 / 文件大、恢复慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序追加每条写命令的日志，重启时重放恢复，相当于 Redis 的 WAL
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is an append-only log of every write command, replayed on restart — Redis's write-ahead log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把写顺序追加到日志再应用，崩溃后靠重放日志恢复
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records each write sequentially before applying it, so a crash recovers by replay.

消费组是 Kafka 独有的能力，Redis Streams 只能单消费者、无法把消息分给多个 worker 并行
两者都有消费组分发多 worker；耐久上 Kafka（磁盘+副本）更抗丢，Redis 内存快但保留有限
Redis 的 XACK 和 Kafka 提交 offset 是毫不相干的两套机制，语义上根本不能类比
options_en: Redis Streams is pure in-memory and loses everything on a crash, so a no-drop case must use Kafka
Consumer groups are Kafka-only; Redis Streams has a single consumer and can't fan out to workers
Both have consumer groups to fan out to workers; on durability Kafka (disk+replicas+long retention) is strongest, Redis is faster but retention is limited
Redis XACK and Kafka offset commit are unrelated mechanisms and can't be compared
optionExplanations: 错：Redis Streams 有 AOF 持久化 + PEL 保住在途消息，不是一崩全丢；只是耐久弱于 Kafka 的磁盘+副本。
错：Redis Streams 有消费组（XREADGROUP GROUP），组内消息按 worker 负载均衡，能并行。
对：这就是本题的取舍点——两者都能分发到多 worker，真正的差别只在耐久强弱。
错：XACK 和提交 offset 语义相同——都是「标记已完成」，不标就会被重投（at-least-once），能类比。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis Streams has AOF persistence + a PEL that keeps in-flight messages — it isn't a total loss on crash; it's just less durable than Kafka's disk+replicas.
Wrong: Redis Streams has consumer groups (XREADGROUP GROUP) that load-balance messages across workers, so it can parallelize.
Right: this is the trade-off — both fan out to workers; the real difference is only how durable each is.
Wrong: XACK and committing an offset mean the same thing — "mark done"; skip it and the message is redelivered (at-least-once), so they are analogous.
why: 两者都用消费组把消息分给不同 worker（Redis XREADGROUP / Kafka partition）。选谁看耐久：Kafka 磁盘+副本可回放、最抗丢单；Redis Streams 内存快、不丢在途(PEL)，但保留受限。
why_en: Both fan out to workers via consumer groups (Redis XREADGROUP / Kafka partition assignment). Pick by durability: Kafka's disk + replicas + long retention + replay make it strongest for 'never drop a request'; Redis Streams is low-latency and doesn't lose in-flight work (PEL) but retention is memory-bound.
tradeoff: Redis Streams（内存·低延迟·保留有限） vs Kafka（磁盘+副本·高耐久·可回放·大吞吐）

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 消费者在某个 partition 里的读取位置；提交 offset = 记下「读到这了」，重启从这继续
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a Kafka consumer's read position in a partition; committing it records progress so restarts resume there.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams 里标记一条消息「已处理完」，从 PEL 移除；作用等价于 Kafka 提交 offset
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK marks a Redis Streams message as processed and removes it from the PEL — analogous to committing a Kafka offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组里「已投递但还没 XACK」的消息列表；worker 死了这些不丢，可被 XAUTOCLAIM 接管重做
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL holds delivered-but-not-yet-acked messages; if a worker dies they survive and can be taken over via XAUTOCLAIM.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka topic 的分区，组内每个分区被一个消费者独占，是并行度与保序的单位（按 key 分区）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is a slice of a Kafka topic; each is consumed by one consumer in a group — the unit of parallelism and per-key ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个逻辑事件类型一个 topic/stream（如 ride-requests 一个）；并行/保序靠 Kafka 的 partition 或 Redis 的多 stream/消费组——不是一个事件一条 stream
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model one topic/stream per logical event type (e.g. one ride-requests); parallelism/ordering comes from Kafka partitions or multiple Redis streams — not one stream per event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 至少一次投递：处理完才确认(ack/commit)，没确认就重投——保证不丢，但可能重复，业务要幂等
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery: a message is redelivered until acknowledged, so nothing is lost but handlers must be idempotent.
